beats.text: Language models can write flawless essays. Yet fail completely when asked to interact with a live database.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard showing an LLM outputting fluent prose on the left, but abruptly crashing into a red blocked API wall on the right.

beats.text: Chain-of-thought models hallucinate inside an isolated vacuum. Pure action agents stumble blindly without an internal plan. Neither can self-correct when API calls break.
beats.visual_focus: Split chalkboard showing CoT spinning in an endless speculative spiral on top, and an Action-only agent blindly firing invalid commands into an error log below.

beats.text: The ReAct framework unifies them. It interleaves reasoning traces directly with real-world tool execution in a continuous feedback cycle.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing nexus pulling the speculative chain of thought and the concrete execution tool into an interlocking triad.

beats.text: First, the model emits a Thought to strategize. Next, it fires an Action to query external APIs. Finally. It ingests the Observation to update its next step.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This was super clean and hit straight to the point. The contrast in Beat 1 between writing essays and failing on a live database is something every dev playing with LLMs has actually experienced. Beat 4 breaks down the Thought-Action-Observation loop clearly without resorting to weird cartoon metaphors or dumbing it down. You kept real terms like 'APIs', 'hallucinate', and 'reinforcement learning baselines' which made it feel legit.
